Add or remove a span processor

Source: R/span-processor.R
add_span_processor.Rd

A span processor is a set of callbacks that otelsdk calls for every span, no matter which package or function created it. You can use a span processor to add attributes to spans that are created by code you do not control, e.g. to add the current user to every span that Shiny creates.

Usage

add_span_processor(on_start = NULL, ..., id = NULL)

remove_span_processor(id)

Arguments

on_start

Function to call when a span starts, or NULL. See details below.

...

Reserved for more callbacks in the future. Must be empty.

id

Id of the span processor, a string. For add_span_processor() it may be NULL, then a new id is generated. If a span processor with the same id already exists, it is replaced. For remove_span_processor() it is the id returned by add_span_processor().

Value

add_span_processor() returns the id of the span processor, invisibly. remove_span_processor() returns TRUE if the span processor was removed and FALSE if there was no span processor with this id, invisibly.

Details

Span processors are part of the OpenTelemetry SDK, not the API, so they are meant to be set up by whoever configures the telemetry output of an app, not by the authors of instrumented packages.

Span processors are global: they apply to the spans of all tracer providers.

Currently span processors only support an on_start callback.

on_start

The on_start callback is called right after a span has started, for every span that is recording. It is called with two arguments:

  • span: the new span, an otel_span object. You can call its methods, e.g. span$set_attribute() or span$set_attributes().

  • info: a named list with more information about the span:

    • name: span name.

    • tracer_name: name of the tracer that created the span. This is usually the name of the instrumented package.

    • kind: span kind, a string.

    • parent: the parent span option, if it was set explicitly when starting the span, or NULL.

The return value of on_start is ignored.

If a callback fails, otelsdk emits an otel_error_message message, and continues with the next span processor. The span is still created. Set the OTEL_ENV=dev environment variable to get errors instead.

If a callback starts a new span, span processors are not called for that span.

Setting up span processors from an environment variable

Use the OTEL_R_SPAN_PROCESSORS environment variable to set up span processors that are defined in packages, without changing the code of the app. It is a comma separated list of pkg::name entries. Each entry must refer to a named list of callbacks, e.g.:

span_processor <- list(
  on_start = function(span, info) {
    span$set_attribute("deployment.region", "eu-west-1")
  }
)

and then

OTEL_R_SPAN_PROCESSORS=mypkg::span_processor

otelsdk reads OTEL_R_SPAN_PROCESSORS when the first span is started. The id of these span processors is env: followed by the entry, e.g. env:mypkg::span_processor.

If the list has callbacks that this version of otelsdk does not support, otelsdk ignores them with a message, and uses the rest of the span processor. This way a package can define callbacks for newer otelsdk versions and still work with older ones.

Example Shiny app

This span processor adds the user and the session token to every span that starts inside a Shiny session:

# Add the Shiny user and session token to every span that Shiny creates
# for this app. See README.md in this directory for how to run it.

library(shiny)

otelsdk::add_span_processor(
  id = "shiny-session",
  on_start = function(span, info) {
    session <- shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
    if (is.null(session)) {
      return()
    }
    user <- if (is.null(session$user)) "anonymous" else session$user
    span$set_attribute("app.user", user)
    span$set_attribute("app.session.token", session$token)
  }
)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Span processor example"),
...

See the full example app, with instructions for running it, in the examples/shiny-span-processor directory of the installed otelsdk package:

system.file(package = "otelsdk", "examples", "shiny-span-processor")

Examples

id <- add_span_processor(
  on_start = function(span, info) {
    span$set_attribute("tracer", info$tracer_name)
  }
)
spns <- with_otel_record({
  trc <- otel::get_tracer("mytracer")
  spn <- trc$start_local_active_span("myspan")
  spn$end()
})
spns$traces$myspan$attributes
#> $tracer
#> [1] "mytracer"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "otel_attributes"
remove_span_processor(id)
